details:
Implementation Plan

Plan for #7387: move the slowest step out of the CI job `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the existing step-move rebalance pattern in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (#7250, #7334, #7366, #7382, #7383)
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one thing: move the job's slowest steps, unchanged and under the same names, into the CI job with the most headroom. It rules out raising `timeout-minutes` and adding job names. Earlier budget-watch fixes did the same thing with an explanatory comment and a changelog fragment, so this plan does too. It adds no dependency and no new interface. Other cleanups stay out (see the duplicate test noted under Risks). Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), keeping CI correct and green comes before broader tidying.

**Automation surface (§20.E)**
- No new script. Only an existing workflow file changes.
- Entry point: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which runs on `pull_request` (every base) and on `push` to `main`, `stable` and `orchestrator/project-*`. The `lint` aggregate job and the `budget-watch` job are unchanged.
- No long-running supervisor is needed (§20.C).
- No database work.
- Nothing to add to `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `changelog.d/7387-ci-heal-job-workflow-heal-step-move.md`

## Functions or modules to implement
Move one step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No code changes.

1. Cut the whole step `- name: Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests` out of job `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`. Today it is the first step after `Install Python CI dependencies`. Keep its `run:` body byte for byte: both pytest lines, including the `# Model-provider outage classifier, tracker and resume (issue #6633).` comment.
2. Paste it into job `tests-promote-stall-and-review` as that job's last step, right after `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)`. The step name and body stay the same. Use two-space YAML indentation, matching the neighbouring steps.
3. Add a comment above the moved step, in the style of the comments at lines ~945-953 and ~1803:
   - it moved from `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`, which took 15m12s of its 20 minutes on main (run 38584572151, budget-watch issue #7387);
   - step timings could not be read when this was planned, so it was picked as the heal job's heaviest step by test count and subprocess count;
   - `tests-promote-stall-and-review` was chosen because none of the five earlier rebalances moved anything into it (#7250 and #7334 went to static-checks, #7366 to heal, #7382 and #7383 to release) and budget-watch has never flagged it;
   - the step needs no git history, Node or prepared `.claude/` live copies, and both jobs use the same depth-1 checkout and the same pip install line.
4. Leave `timeout-minutes`, job ids, the `lint` aggregate's `needs:` and every other step unchanged.
5. Add the changelog fragment, in the same `<!-- changelog: changed -->` format and voice as `changelog.d/7383-ci-heal-job-rebalance.md`. It names the moved step, the source and destination jobs, the run, and why the destination was chosen. It ends with "What this means for operators: nothing to change; no new variable."

## Data structures affected
None. Only the step order inside two jobs of `ci.yml` changes.

## API or interface changes
None:
- The required check `CI / lint` is unchanged.
- No job is added or renamed, and no step is renamed.
- A failure in the workflow-heal or provider-outage tests will now show up under the `tests-promote-stall-and-review` check-run instead of `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`.

## Decisions
### D1 — Which step to move
- Chosen: `Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests`, and only that step.
- Alternatives considered:
  - `Unblock judge and scan tests (replace-claude-sessions Phase 7)`: 303 tests, 22 subprocess call sites.
  - Several of the smaller steps.
  - Moving both large steps.
- Why: Step timings could not be read (no `gh` and no network in planning). By static size it is the heaviest step by a wide margin: 8 test files, about 439 test functions, and about 157 `subprocess` call sites, of which `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` alone has 297 tests and 88 sites, and `tests/test_heal_isolated_editor.py` has 42 sites. The job has been flagged four times (#7250, #7334, #7383, #7387). Each earlier fix moved other steps out, and the job came back to about 15 minutes every time. #7383 moved three steps and the job only went from 15m19s to 15m12s. That points to this step as the one taking the time. Moving both large steps into one job could push that job past budget-watch's 15-minute warning.

### D2 — Which job to move it to
- Chosen: `tests-promote-stall-and-review`.
- Alternatives considered:
  - `tests-release-and-log-analysis`: the destination of #7382 and #7383. It measured 535-604s before it took on `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)` and three more steps.
  - `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`: about 15m09s minus six moved steps.
  - `static-checks`: 15-minute budget, already over in #7382.
  - The `orchestrate-poll` matrix: a step there runs four times unless gated on the group index.
- Why: It is the only test job that has received no moved steps and has never been flagged. Every other choice is close to its budget or would duplicate the work.

### D3 — No new regression test
- Chosen: rely on the existing contract tests.
- Alternatives considered: a test that pins this step to a particular job.
- Why: `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py` already enforces that each step runs in exactly one job, that every job sets itself up and has a budget of 20 minutes or less, and that `lint` depends on every job. Pinning the job would make the next rebalance harder. None of the five earlier rebalances added such a pin.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: unchanged. Both jobs run with the same default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions, the same `actions/checkout@v5` (default depth, credentials as before), the same `setup-python@v6` and the same pip install line. The moved step reads no secrets and no `${{ }}` expressions.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface.
- External input: none added. The step body is copied verbatim.
- Abuse cases:
  - A PR that weakens the moved tests is still caught by `lint`'s `needs:` covering `tests-promote-stall-and-review`, which `test_lint_needs_every_other_job` pins.
  - Dropping the step instead of moving it would fail `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`, because each of its eight test files must still be named in some workflow.

## Risks and edge cases
- **No measured timings.** Step timings for run 38584572151 could not be read: `gh` is not installed in the planning sandbox and web access is off, and pytest is not installed locally. D1 and D2 rest on static size and on the record of earlier rebalances. If `tests-promote-stall-and-review` crosses 15 minutes on main, budget-watch opens a new deduplicated `kind=job_duration` issue. That warning does not turn CI red; only the 20-minute timeout does.
- **Line-by-line identity.** The moved block must keep each line identical except for the new comment above it. `test_no_step_runs_in_more_than_one_job` fails if the old copy is left behind.
- **Pinned job of an earlier move.** `tests/test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py` pins the inventory-parity step and the coverage-gate steps to a shared job. Neither is touched here.
- **Workflow size.** `ci.yml` is 107,700 bytes, far below the 480,000-byte guard. The change adds about 10 comment lines.
- **Observation, out of scope.** `tests/test_render_validation_templates_shell_quoting.py` runs in two places: the heal job's `Validation shell-quoting and credential-scrub tests` and promote's `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)`. Removing the duplicate would save a little time, but it changes a step body, which the issue forbids. It is left as is.
- **Conflict with the issue text: none.** The job name, the step names and the 20-minute budget all match the repository.

## Testing considerations
- `python3 tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py`: no step runs in two jobs, every job sets itself up first, budgets are at most 20 minutes, `lint` needs every job.
- `python3 tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`: all eight moved test files are still referenced.
- `python3 tests/test_ci_inventory_parity_order_contract.py` and `python3 tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py`: unchanged contracts still pass.
- `yamllint` and `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the same as the `static-checks` steps.
- `python3 scripts/assemble_changelog.py` dry check / `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py` for the new fragment.
- After merge, check the next `main` CI run: `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` should drop well under 15 minutes, and `tests-promote-stall-and-review` should stay under 15.

## Pre-execution self-check
- The only files that change are `ci.yml` and a changelog fragment. No timeout is raised, no job is added or renamed, and step names and bodies are unchanged. This meets every constraint in the issue.
- Every claimed fact comes from files read during planning: the step list, the earlier changelog fragments, the contract test constants, and the test-file sizes.
- The planning ref is `main` at `bed4bf99ebc824fe89895c1165cb00e7d60b4e87`. `Integration branch mismatch: unknown`, not `true`, so the plan is not blocked.

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: WARNING: Step timings for run 38584572151 could not be read (no `gh` or network in planning, no local pytest), so the step and destination were chosen from static test size and the record of earlier rebalances, not measured durations.
